== Biography ==
'''Isabella Glasgow''' was an adult by 5 March 1600 and was married to [[Howe-15840|John Howe]], a dyer and citizen of Glasgow. On that date protocol 3637 records the spouses selling a workshop, waste ground and stable in a great Briggate tenement which John Hamilton had set in feu to the couple.<ref name="Howe1600">Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 11, protocol 3637, 5 March 1600, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc00renwgoog/page/144/mode/1up p. 145].</ref> This directly proves their marriage, John's occupation and their joint property, but it names neither of Isabella's parents.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1097]] is assessed at 18% (uncertain). Inherited uncertain attachment to Archibald; current findings identify no leading father or property/personal bridge to Isabella. Archibald’s c 1525 generation could father Isabella c 1560, but no positive personal or property association selects him over the other Glasgow adults.

A weak retained attachment. Robert’s David Howe contacts do not repair it, because Isabella’s dyer husband belongs to a different proved Howe household.

Next useful test: Test Isabella’s property title for a named Glasgow predecessor or relative.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-3026 WikiTree profile export for Glasgow-3026]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.



=== Parentage ===
The attached father, [[Glasgow-1097|Archibald Glasgow]], remains uncertain. A search of the published Glasgow protocols for 1530–1600 found no act calling Isabella a daughter, sister or heir of Archibald, Robert, William or another Glasgow. No present candidate has a demonstrated property, inheritance or personal link to her.

[[Glasgow-1096|Robert Glasgow]] was previously treated as the leading alternative because Robert Glesgw twice appeared with David Howe in 1557 and 1559/60.<ref>Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 2, protocol 372, 26 July 1557, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc08scogoog/page/n51/mode/1up protocol abstract]; protocols 525–526, 20 February 1559/60, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc08scogoog/page/n93/mode/1up protocol abstracts].</ref> A fuller Howe reconstruction removes most of that inference. On 25 August 1582 Peter Howie, dyer, and Isobella Maxwell expressly called a John Howee their son; the following act names their other son Umphrid. David Howie, expressly the son of the late William Howie, witnessed John's transaction.<ref name="Howe1582">Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 8, protocols 2448–2449, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc00scogoog/page/n78/mode/2up p. 64], 25 August 1582.</ref>

The 1582 John is probably Isabella's husband: exact name and city, suitable chronology, and the son of a dyer was himself styled dyer in 1600. A different contemporary John Howe is separately styled fisher and married to Marion Park. The probable parentage of Isabella's husband places him in Peter Howie and Isobella Maxwell's household, not David Howe's proved household. Robert Glasgow's association with David therefore does not materially support Robert as Isabella's father.

Robert Herbertson's appearance as a witness to the 1600 transaction does not establish that Isabella was related to [[Herbison-439|Margaret Herbesoun]].
